terms.gloss: say hello to Marcus for me
evidence: Cic. Att. 4.14.2, cited by L&S: Dionysium jubē salvēre

terms.grammar: salūtem, accusative of salūs, with dīcere and the dative of the person greeted
evidence: Cic. Att. 14.19.6: tū Atticae salūtem dīcēs (Lewis & Short), s.v. salūs
Cic. Fam. 14.7.3: salūtem plūrimam dīcit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The opening of a Roman letter, S. D. (salūtem dīcit), and the way to pass on someone’s greetings: Terentia tibi salūtem dīcit.

evidence: Plaut. Poen. 1.2.194: multam salūtem dīcere alicui, to greet heartily (Lewis & Short s.v. multus)
Cic. Att. 2.12.4: Terentia impertit tibi multam salūtem (Lewis & Short s.v. impertiō)
Traupman 106: give him (her) my best regards, dīcitō eī multam meīs verbīs salūtem
terms.comment: Meīs verbīs, “in my words”, is “from me”: Piliam meīs verbīs cōnsōlēre (Cic. Att. 5.11.7, Lewis & Short s.v. cōnsōlor).

phrases.english: Say hello to Grandma for me!

phrases.latin: Atticae, quoniam, quod optimum in puerīs est, hilarula est, meīs verbīs suāvium dēs volō.
phrases.english: Give Attica a kiss from me, since she is cheerful, the best thing in children.

phrases.latin: Dīcitō eī multam meīs verbīs salūtem.
